questions.q: In alkaline medium, the reduction of permanganate anion involves a gain of ____________ electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In Faintly alkaline medium potassium permanganate changes to manganese dioxide in its oxidising action.

MnO4-+2H2O+3e-→MnO2+4OH-

The oxidation state of manganese in MnO4- is +7 and in MnO2 is +4.

Hence, it transfers 3 electrons during the oxidising action in alkaline medium.

questions.q:
See the following chemical reaction:

Cr2O72-+XH++6Fe2+→YCr3++6Fe3++ZH2O

The sum of X, Y and Z is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given equation can be balanced using ion-electron method as shown below.

Fe2+→Fe3++e-         -oxidation Half reaction

6e-+14H++Cr2O72-→2Cr3++7H2O -Reduction Half reaction

The overall reaction is 

6Fe2++14H++Cr2O72-→6Fe3++2Cr3++7H2O

The values X=14,Y=2 and Z = 7

(X+ Y +Z)  = 14 + 2 +7

= 23

questions.q:
2MnO4-+bC2O42-+cH+→xMn2++yCO2+zH2O
If the above equation is balanced with integer coefficients, the value of c is _______ . (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Writing the half reaction

Reduction half reaction 

MnO4-→Mn2+

balancing oxygen 

MnO4-→Mn2++4H2O

balancing Hydrogen 

8H++MnO4-→Mn2++4H2O

balancing charge 

5e-+8H++MnO4-→Mn2++4H2O

Oxidation half 

C2O42-→CO2
Balancing carbon

C2O42-→2CO2

Balancing charge

C2O42-→2CO2+2e-

Net equation

16H++2MnO4-+5C2O42-→10CO2+2Mn2++8H2O

So c=16

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Titration principle is N1V1=N2V2

N = Normality

V = Volume of solution

M1V1n1=M2V2n2

M = molarity

n = Valence factor of acid or base

As pink colour is obtained on consumption of 10 ml of Ca(OH)2, we have

20×0.5×1=10×M×2

Molarity of Ca(OH)2=1020=12M

Also, moles of Ca(OH)2=mm of H2SO4

12×20=10×M

Molarity of H2SO4=1M

2MnO4-+4H2O+6e-→2MnO2+8OH-

Oxidation Half reaction

2I-→I2+2e-

6I-→3I2+6e-

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
50ml of 0.5 M oxalic acid is completely neutralised by 25ml of NaOH solution. 

For neutralisation reactions, N1V1=N2V2

Normality of oxalic acid = Molarity×2

⇒Noxalic acid=0.5×2=1N

50×1=25×NNaOH

For sodium hydroxide, molarity is the same as normality.

Molarity of sodium hydroxide = 2M

The number of moles of sodium hydroxide= 50×2×10-3 mol.

Hence, the mass of sodium hydroxide =50×2×10-3×40=4g
